test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 12 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The erstwhile state of Bombay was bifurcated to create the present-day states of Maharashtra and ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **On May 1, 1960, Bombay State **was abolished and divided into** the states of Gujarat, **which has a majority **Gujarati-speaking population, and Maharashtra,** which has a **majority Marathi-speaking population.**
 
• At the time of India's independence, a sizable Indian state called Bombay State was established, and other districts were later added to it.
 
• Bombay Presidency was combined with the princely states of Baroda, Western India, Gujarat (the modern Indian state of Gujarat), and the Deccan States.
 
• Bombay Presidency roughly corresponds to the modern Indian state of Maharashtra, except for South Maharashtra and Vidarbha (which included parts of the present-day Indian states of Maharashtra and Karnataka).
 
• **The Saurashtra and Kutch States,** which ceased to exist, were absorbed into Bombay State on November 1 as part of the States Reorganisation Act's linguistic reorganisation of states. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Kannada-speaking areas of Belgaum (apart from Chandgad Taluka), Bijapur, Dharwar, and North Canara **were moved from** Bombay State to Mysore State **as a result of the States Reorganisation Act on November 1st, 1956.
 
• The Marathi-speaking Marathwada portion of Hyderabad State, the Marathi-speaking Vidarbha region of southern Madhya Pradesh, and the Gujarati-speaking Saurashtra and Kutch states were all added to the State of Bombay, which was also greatly expanded.
